summary: Offshore light on a shoal off Cheboygan, first exhibited in 1930 and built to be run by radio from Poe Reef; sources disagree on whether a keeper was ever assigned.

lens.where: Replaced in 1956 by a 200 mm drum lens lantern (LighthouseFriends); archive lists a 250 mm current optic

structures.type: conical cast-iron tower on a steel house
structures.note: Archive: 55 ft from base to lantern center. Station on a timber crib filled with concrete; steel house and conical tower on the deck. Pepper describes the tower as a steel cylinder with a cast-iron lantern.

staffing.note: Pepper says no keeper was ever assigned. The 1930 Bulletin says one keeper was provided. LighthouseFriends says the single keeper was withdrawn for the 1935 season.

access.note: Reached by boat only; tower closed (LighthouseFriends). The archive lists it as not open to the public.

facts.owner: Disputed in the sources read: LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard owns it and also reports a 2017 GSA auction; the buyer is not named in any source read

events.note: Acetylene gas buoy replaced the can buoy marking the shoal, 15 April 1925
Timber crib built onshore July 1928 and towed out the following month
Concrete deck and steel house finished; lantern room installed by 3 October 1929
Placed in commission at the opening of navigation; LighthouseFriends gives 18 April 1930
Cheboygan Point light discontinued the same season
Single keeper withdrawn at the opening of navigation (LighthouseFriends quoting the Lake Carriers' Association report for 1935)
Fourth-order lens replaced by a 200 mm drum lens lantern (LighthouseFriends)
Repainted and refurbished by the crew of the USCGC Mackinaw (LighthouseFriends)

GSA online auction, opened 25 July 2017; closed 30 September 2017 with a high bid of $133,333 (LighthouseFriends). Buyer not named in sources read

corrections.why: No source read supports 1848. The archive gives 1930 as the year established and the tower; Pepper, LighthouseFriends and the 1930 Bulletin all date the first exhibition to the 1930 opening of navigation. Human review needed to find where the 1848 date came from.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1848 date is not supported by any source read. The archive, Pepper, LighthouseFriends and the 1930 Bulletin all give 1930. The story uses 1930.

Pepper gives a 50-foot focal plane; LighthouseFriends, quoting the Commissioner's report, gives 51 feet above water. The record's 15.5 m (51 ft) matches the Commissioner's figure. The story gives no focal height.

Pepper says no keeper was ever assigned (the light was run from Poe Reef). The 1930 Bulletin says the station was provided with one keeper. LighthouseFriends, quoting the Lake Carriers' Association report, says a single keeper was retained until the opening of navigation in 1935. No keeper is named in any source read. The story states all three accounts.

LighthouseFriends' visitor notes say the Coast Guard owns the light, while its history reports the 2017 GSA auction (high bid $133,333) without naming the buyer. The story states both and does not settle the owner.

The archive record gives the location as 'Cheboygan Harbor Entrance/Lake Michigan'. Pepper and LighthouseFriends place the light off Cheboygan, and the 1925 and 1930 Bulletins place the station in the Straits of Mackinac. The story says Straits of Mackinac and does not repeat the archive's lake label.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the archive lists none. Pepper says no keeper was ever assigned. The 1930 Bulletin says the station was provided with one keeper. LighthouseFriends says a single keeper stayed until 1935, quoting the Lake Carriers' Association report for that year; that report was not read directly. No keeper's name appears in any source read. Human check: 2017 GSA auction result. LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard owns the light and also reports the auction, and no source read names the buyer. Check the GSA sale record. Tower material: the record says concrete. Pepper says a steel cylinder with a cast-iron lantern; LighthouseFriends says a conical cast-iron tower on a steel house; the archive says reinforced concrete and steel. The sources read do not settle it. Characteristic: the record gives 'Oc W 4s'. Pepper describes the 1930 light as a single one-second flash every three seconds. The current characteristic is not confirmed from the Light List. Lens: LighthouseFriends says a 200 mm drum lens replaced the fourth-order lens in 1956; the archive's current optic is 250 mm. Not read: the USCG Historian's entry (archived copies would not load in this pass); Commissioner of Lighthouses reports for 1928 to 1935 (not in the local corpus); Lake Carriers' Association reports (quoted second-hand). Newspapers: no Michigan hits for Fourteen Foot Shoal in Chronicling America, 1925 to 1940. The story is short because the sources give no keeper names and no recorded wrecks or rescues at the station. Copyright: LighthouseFriends and Pepper are all-rights-reserved sites; the story uses facts in our own words, with a few short quotations of one to nine words (Pepper twice, the 1930 Bulletin once). Fact check 2026-10-22: the 1930 tonnage is on Bulletin PDF p. 19 (new source 8), not p. 18; the $78,000 appropriation is LighthouseFriends only, not the 1929 Bulletin; the station's keeper accounts and the owner dispute are now stated in the story; the archive's 'Lake Michigan' location label is not repeated.
